Your Mac has 6 screenshot shortcuts, and most of the mess on your desktop comes from using only 1.

#1 Whole screen: Command Shift 3
#2 A part: Command Shift 4 (hold Space to move the box)
#3 1 window: Command Shift 4, then Space (Option to drop the shadow)
#4 Record the screen: Command Shift 5
#5 Copy instead of save: add Control
#6 Change where they go: Command Shift 5, Options, Save to

Friday night I couldn't read a notification on my own Lock Screen. White text, right on top of a white beach photo.

That's Liquid Glass. iOS 27 added a slider for it:
Settings, Appearance, Liquid Glass. Drag right for tinted, left for clear.

Still too busy? Settings, Accessibility, Display & Text Size, Reduce Transparency.

My phone rang. Caller ID said my bank. He knew my name, the last 4 digits of my card, even my last purchase. And he wanted my savings moved to a "safe account". Right now.

Face ID can't stop that, because it really is you tapping send.

iOS 27 added a check for exactly that moment, and it ships switched off. Settings, Privacy & Security, Impersonation Risk Detection, then turn on Share with App Developers. When a supported banking app sees you sending money or changing a password, it can ask your iPhone if this looks like a scam. The app gets only a risk level, never your messages or photos.

Has a fake "bank" ever called you or someone in your family? Tell me in the comments.

Save this and turn it on for your parents tonight.

I turned my ringer almost all the way down so a 2 AM call wouldn't wake anyone. My 6:30 alarm came out as a whisper. I slept right through it.

On iPhone, your alarm has always followed your ringer volume. Turn one down and the other goes down with it.

iOS 27 finally splits them. Settings, Sounds & Haptics, then under Alarms turn off Match Ringtone Volume. Your alarm gets its own slider.

Has your alarm ever failed you like this? Tell me what happened in the comments.

Save this and check your alarm before tonight.

My iPhone hit 20% by lunch and I had barely touched it. These 3 settings were part of the reason.

#1 Adaptive Power: Settings, Battery, Power Mode. Makes small cuts like a slightly dimmer screen on heavy days. iPhone 15 Pro and newer.
#2 Limit Frame Rate: Settings, Accessibility, Motion. Caps the screen at 60 Hz on ProMotion iPhones.
#3 Keyboard haptics: Settings, Sounds & Haptics, Keyboard Feedback, then turn off Haptic. Apple says it can affect battery life.

Messy website? Your iPhone already has the fix. 3 Safari buttons, all in the Page Menu.

#1 Hide Distracting Items: tap a banner or popup and it disappears
#2 Show Reader: just the words and photos, nothing else
#3 Listen to Page: Safari reads the article out loud while you do something else

To open the Page Menu, tap the button at the left of the address bar. Hide Distracting Items needs iOS 18 or later. To bring hidden items back, open the Page Menu and tap Show Hidden Items.
